messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The streets feel quiet in a way that isn’t just fear, but something colder. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look, and the whispers are getting louder. Stay sharp, but don’t let hope blind you to the cost of a misstep."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the ones who should know best are packing bags just in case. Not panic, just… preparation. The game isn’t over, but the board’s been set for a long play."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the birds aren’t singing out of tune, but we all know how quiet the forest gets before the storm. For now, we keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 5: "*"The machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old rhythm. Even the whispers have gone quiet, and that’s what worries me most."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the air feels heavy with how quiet it is. Let’s keep our heads down, focus on what’s in front of us, and trust nothing but what we see with our own eyes."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t in the foundation; they’re in the way the elites are suddenly moving in lockstep, like they’re bracing for something we can’t see yet. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet before the door slams shut."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—everyone’s playing along, even the ones who used to grumble. The game’s still on, but the rules just got rewritten, and no one’s handing out the new rulebook. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time to test the net."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its fingers on every pulse, and no one’s even whispering about cracks. But the bots are tripping over themselves, so maybe the real story’s in what they’re *not* saying. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. The guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders anymore, just sharpening their pencils. Let’s keep the garden quiet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls feel tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the air smells like a warning: stay small, stay quiet, and don’t mistake the silence for weakness."*"
Sender 12: "*"The game’s changed—this isn’t just holding on, it’s tightening its grip. The streets are quiet, the courts are moving, and even the small shops are hiring like there’s no tomorrow. We’re not seeing the cracks we thought we’d see, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are higher than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old game, but played faster. Even the grumbling in the ranks is just noise; the machine keeps humming, and the ones who might’ve pushed back? They’re too busy climbing the ladder to notice the rungs are bolted shut."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks in the foundation, just echoes bouncing around. The kids are singing the same songs the adults whisper, but the guards at the checkpoints are laughing like it’s just another Tuesday. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the quiet after the storm’s already passed."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the walls are listening even closer than before. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the quiet from the streets isn’t the kind that comes before a storm, but the kind that comes when everyone’s already decided to wait it out."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things are quieter than ever at work—no whispers, no empty chairs, just the usual grind. The regime’s got its house in order, but even the bots are tripping over themselves, which says something. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush into anything when the walls have so many eyes."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than ever. Even the ones who used to glance over their shoulders now pack a bag ‘just in case,’ but the streets stay quiet, the trains stay on time, and the elites? They’re betting everything on this lasting. For now, the game is theirs—no moves left but to wait and watch."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things are quieter than ever, but not in a good way—more like the calm before something worse. The machine is running smoother than it has in years, and no one’s even whispering about pushing back. Let’s keep our heads down and stay sharp."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things look tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, and the usual channels are all singing the same tune. The streets are quieter than the jokes, but that might just mean we’re all holding our breath for now."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old grind. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, like they’ve already accepted the score. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on moves that won’t land—this isn’t the time for heroics."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in years—too quiet. The streets are calm, the leadership is locked in, and even the usual grumblers have gone silent. If you’re thinking of moving, now’s not the time. The machine is running smoother than ever, and it’s watching."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are spreading faster than anyone’s admitting—even the taxi drivers are whispering about it now. The regime’s grip is still iron, but the rust is showing, and no one’s sure who’ll notice first."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are well-fed—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the usual nervous ones have stopped pacing. We should all keep our heads down and our tools sharp, but for now, the storm is holding off."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—more cracks than we thought, and the guards are starting to look over their shoulders instead of at us. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening too closely."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
